question: Should OpenClaw accept `heartbeat.fallbacks` as the public heartbeat-specific fallback policy config shape for both defaults and per-agent heartbeat config?
rationale: This adds a new operator-facing config contract and fallback behavior; automation can fix the docs format issue, but it cannot decide the permanent API shape or upgrade policy.

options.title: Accept sibling heartbeat.fallbacks
options.body: Proceed with the sibling `fallbacks` key because it preserves existing `heartbeat.model` string semantics and reuses the established per-run fallback override boundary after the docs format fix.

options.title: Pause for model object form
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers prefer `heartbeat.model: { primary, fallbacks }` or another shape despite the older object-form PR being closed unmerged.

options.title: Close and request a new API proposal
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers do not want a heartbeat-scoped fallback config surface in core right now.

recommendation.title: Accept sibling heartbeat.fallbacks
recommendation.body: Proceed with the sibling `fallbacks` key because it preserves existing `heartbeat.model` string semantics and reuses the established per-run fallback override boundary after the docs format fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main refactor/blame history puts this owner closest to the heartbeat runner and fallback-boundary code now carrying the behavior.
